title: 7.5x Sharper Non-Scalar Border-Rank Constant (4 q_ns), Exact Single-Gate Border-Rank Tightness via Strassen's Equation, and Sharp Bilinear/PIT Verification Bounds
abstract: Chen Xiangle (arXiv:2611.34814v1, Theorem 1) recently proved that any deterministic real arithmetic decision tree of cost s verifying a bilinear map T : R^p x R^q -> R^m yields the border-rank upper bound brank_R(T) <= 30s, implying that deterministic verification and computation of n x n matrix products share the same arithmetic exponent omega_v = omega_C. Here we sharpen both the quantitative constant and the algebraic complexity model of Chen's framework, and establish exact tightness, finite-size, and field-dependence boundaries. First (Theorem 1), by initializing the Baur-Strassen reverse pass directly via bar{z}_j += 2 z_j (making all equality/inequality tests and all linear gates completely free), exploiting implicit differentiation for unsplit division gates, constructing an exact 4-term Walsh-Hadamard polarization identity for the 3x3x3 single-gate forward-reverse tensor G_3, and applying double-limit diagonalization to the border-rank-2 squaring tensor G_sq, we collapse Chen's 30s bound to the Ostrowski-Strassen non-scalar inequality brank_C(T) <= brank_R(T) <= 4(q_mul + q_div) + 2 q_sq <= 4 q_ns <= 4s, achieving a universal 7.5x reduction (15x on squaring circuits, 35.4x on Strassen 2x2 verifiers). Using Strassen's commutator equation on A = J_3 - I_3, we prove brank_C(G_3) = rank_R(G_3) = 4 and brank_C(G_sq) = 2 < 3 = rank_R(G_sq), establishing unconditional border-rank tightness for gate-by-gate tensor decompositions. Second (Theorem 2), we derive sharper finite-size non-scalar verification lower bounds q_ns(M_n) >= ceil(brank_C(M_n)/4) (lowering the conditional omega_C = 9/4 Freivalds crossover dimension by 50625/16 approx 3164x, from 12,960,000 to 4096) and halve the mixed-derivative error constant of Chen's Lemma 3 from 2 tau to tau via symmetric diagonal polarization along the exact Pareto frontier (delta^theta, O(delta^{(1-theta)/2})). Third (Theorem 3), we prove that Chen's dense quadratic PIT upper bound S^{omega_C/2 + o(1)} is attained uniquely at the square aspect ratio d = 2K (alpha = 1) with strict rectangular exponent savings |alpha-1|(omega_C-2)/(2(1+alpha)) for all alpha != 1, prove that Chen's univariate sum-of-squares reduction (Proposition 5(ii)) and real Gram reduction fail over every finite field F_p and over C, and tighten complex-to-real pair simulation constants via Gauss's 3-multiplication identity. All algebraic identities, commutator minors, dual-number executions, and finite-size tables are machine-verified by 20 constructive, dependency-free Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice), 16 zero-float SHA-256 rational certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
